Command: Stand Fast in the Liberty of Christ
Summary: Paul's liberty command: stand fast in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
Commandment: Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
Application: Liberty is not licence but freedom from law-keeping as the way of standing with God. Returning to circumcision as a requirement would entangle the Galatians again — Christ would profit them nothing on those terms.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage' (Galatians 5:1).
Function: Liberty is not licence but freedom from law-keeping as the way of standing with God. The apostles gave this one, not Moses — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal was to keep the Galatians from being entangled again with the yoke of bondage — circumcision as a requirement, on whose terms Christ would profit them nothing. The evil it addressed was return to bondage, freedom surrendered for the safety of rules. It restrained that evil by the stand itself: stand fast in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free.
